title: Choose the look of the browser window
question: The roll assigned Index-Tab Notebook. Colours in every card are a sample wallpaper; in the browser they are derived from your real wallpaper. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Index-Tab Notebook
options.lineage: Japanese campus notebooks with coloured index dividers
options.thesis: Folders are coloured divider tabs and workspaces are binder tabs, on a calm matte ground tinted by your wallpaper.
options.viewport: Sidebar holds a rounded address pill, a tab list where a folder is a colour-keyed divider with its tabs indented under it, and three binder tabs above the footer.
options.risk: Divider and binder shapes can look fussy if the colours are not restrained.

raised.raise: One strict text size in the sidebar; hierarchy comes only from weight and fill.

options.label: Wallpaper-Lit Glass
options.lineage: Big Sur / Arc translucent sidebars over the desktop picture
options.thesis: The sidebar is frosted glass lit by your wallpaper, and the page floats above it as one soft card.
options.viewport: Translucent sidebar with a pill address bar, light-filled active tab, small-caps folder labels, pill workspace dots, and a shadowed page card.
options.risk: Familiar, and blur behind the sidebar is not verified on this compositor yet.

options.label: Midnight Transit Lines
options.lineage: metropolitan rail diagrams on midnight enamel
options.thesis: Tabs are stations on a line, a folder is a branch, and each workspace is a coloured line.
options.viewport: A vertical line with station dots for tabs, an amber branch for the folder, and three coloured workspace line chips.
options.case: Strong audience fit (workspaces as lines) but a saturated ground fights the wallpaper-tinted palette.
options.risk: Costume risk if the line motif becomes decoration instead of structure.

options.label: Dense Modules
options.thesis: Small type, hairline boxes and one red tab per module pack the sidebar like a control panel.
options.viewport: Boxed address bar, ruled tab rows 24 px high, a red folder tab and a segmented workspace strip.
options.case: Shows the most tabs per screen, but it is bright, severe, and ignores the wallpaper.
options.risk: Too busy for hours of daily use.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.case: Raked slanted panes fight a native vertical list.
options.kept: One strict text size, rank by weight only.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.case: Cream and serif is the default rendition and has nothing to do with browsing.
options.kept: Fixed scale and a shared baseline.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the whole screen.
options.case: Chrome would disappear, which a browser cannot do.
options.kept: The page as the single hero.

options.label: Variable Specimen
options.case: Reads as a type foundry, not a browser.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean flat vertical-tabs browser, executed well.
canonCard.viewport: Flat dark sidebar, grey pills, blue folder labels, white page card with small radius.
